To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: [ACTION] Production swap: gating criteria, enablement & docs sync

Team,

We have a tentative production swap window on 2026-09-24 between 02:00-04:00 UTC (US-first roll). Before we flip traffic I need sign-off on three buckets: 1) gating criteria (SLOs, canary pass/fail), 2) enablement (support runbooks + CS training), and 3) docs & communications (customer-facing changelog + internal runbooks).

Please respond with the status below by EOD PDT today:
- Product: Are there remaining product exceptions or feature flags that block the swap? Who owns the doc updates?
- Engineering/Infra: Canary plan confirmation, capacity checks, special handling for Dedicated/Private accounts. Link infra ticket if created.
- Support/CS: Training slots and runbook readiness (post-swap rollback steps).
- Sales/Leadership: Any customer-level exceptions we need to carve out (audit/logging, retention).

I've attached the current prod_swap_checklist_v3.xlsx and the draft canary_policy.md. Also linking the shared folder with runbooks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cProdSwapDocs

If you need to defer, say what the blocker is and propose an explicit mitigation. Acme, looping you in for visibility — any constraints on your side?

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Dylan —

Quick updates from Product:
- Feature flags: We have three new flags for the swap (fee_optimizations, kv_cache_hotfix, fallback_model_v2). All are in a locked state and the rollout plan is in the spreadsheet (owners column).
- Exceptions: There is one known exception — a small schema delta for our logging pipeline that requires a DB migration. Migration is low-risk but we need a 1-hour freeze window and an explicit canary in EU before global rollout. I'm attaching the migration plan.
- Docs: I will own the customer-facing changelog and have drafted the bullet points; internal API docs will be updated by Dev and Jonas. ETA for docs updates: 9/23 EOD.

Proposed gating criteria (high level):
- Canary success: 1% traffic for 30m with error rate <0.3% and P95 latency within baseline + 20%.
- No SEV>2 incidents in the 24h after canary.
- DB migration must complete and be validated on staging/EU canary.

I'll be available on the 24th for the swap and monitoring.

-Ava
Ava Chen

Dylan/Ava —

Engineering status:
- Canary policy: confirmed. I've reviewed canary_policy.md and pushed a minor clarification to the failure thresholds (see INF-4827).
- Capacity: We've run a 2x load test on staging for the new model variant; memory/throughput look good. Dedicated pools for existing customers were tested and passed autoscale checks.
- Private customers: note that Private v1 clusters need a small runtime config tweak (KV cache size) which I will roll out in a targeted canary on 9/23 22:00 UTC. This is low-risk but will require a short maintenance window for those tenants — I've added a note to the checklist.
- Tickets: INF-4827 (canary thresholds), INF-4832 (private-kv-cache).

I'll be on-call for the swap. If the DB migration is a blocker, I recommend we schedule the EU canary early and gate global traffic until we have green metrics.

-Dev
